hints.title: Bounded Horizon Predecessor Optimization
hints.text: To reach step i with maximum score, one should jump from the predecessor index j in [i - k, i - 1] that achieved the largest score.

hints.title: Decreasing Sliding Deque Invariant
hints.text: The optimal previous jump score is always held at the front of a monotonic double-ended queue maintained in strictly decreasing order.

hints.title: Sliding Maximum DP Procedure
hints.text: Maintain a deque storing indices. Seed with index 0. For each position i from 1 to n - 1, discard indices outside the k-window from the front. Compute dp[i] = nums[i] + dp[dq[0]]. Evict indices from the rear whose dp values are less than or equal to dp[i], append index i, and return dp[n - 1].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input length or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(K) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recomputing the maximum of the prior k values at every step takes O(N * K) time, timing out for N = 100,000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A monotonic deque tracks the window maximum in O(1) amortized time per step and O(K) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize dynamic programming combined with a monotonic deque to maintain the maximum score within the k-jump window.
